name: Glacier Terminus
desc: The calving face of a tidewater glacier — three ranks of ice stand out of black water, seracs sawtooth the crest, annual stratification dips across the wall and crevasses open into englacial blue that gets deeper the further in you look, while brash ice and growlers drift out on the current and katabatic mist pours off the foot; an overcast terminus, the blue hour, a filthy ablating face, an InSAR velocity interferogram, or an iridescent thin-film shell.

energy.doc: how hard the light works — spray, water contrast, ambient glow off the ice

scale.doc: how monumental the face is — wall height, serac and crevasse size (rebuilds every face)

density.doc: how many crevasses, stratification bands, swell lines and floes

speed.doc: mist scroll, floe drift and calving rate

crevasse.doc: how badly the ice is broken — 0 is a sound wall, 1 is a shattered chaos of seracs

brash.doc: how much broken ice is in the water at the foot of the face

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default cold ice-blue

x.doc: which way the light rakes — which lip of each crevasse is lit

y.doc: the waterline at the foot of the face — low y gives more water and more drifting ice

style.doc: aesthetic: terminus = overcast calving face, cold white ice, englacial blue, black water; bluehour = twilight, the ice is the only thing left with light in it; moraine = a filthy ablating face, heavy sediment banding, the ice losing; interferogram = an InSAR velocity map where rainbow fringes encode surface displacement rather than light; nacre = the face as an iridescent thin-film oil-slick shell, no ice colour at all

act.doc: multi-minute programme — the ice creeping, blocks shearing off the face, or a hard freeze locking the water

seed.doc: regenerates the seracs, crevasse field, stratification and floes

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
